messages:
Nora (People Ops): Quick policy drop: today we're launching two related updates effective 2026-11-01: (1) a PTO Donation Program (PDO) so employees can donate unused PTO to colleagues facing hardship, and (2) enhanced lactation accommodations (flex scheduling + dedicated nursing room reservations). Docs & request forms in the links below.

Luis (People Ops): PDO basics: employees can donate up to 40 hours/year; donations go into a team-specific pool and can be requested by eligible recipients who need extra paid time for serious personal/family hardship. Donations are voluntary and anonymous to recipients.

Aisha (Eng Manager): How does eligibility work for recipients? We sometimes get requests for gap coverage that aren't medical per se.

Nora (People Ops): Eligibility is for documented hardship (medical, caregiving crisis, natural disaster impact). Managers submit a confidential request on behalf of the employee; People Ops reviews within 3 business days. We're intentionally narrow to prevent mission creep.

Ravi (Legal): Donation tax/comp treatment: donated hours are not taxable income to recipients, but payroll must track the source hours for recordkeeping. Donors retain normal taxable status (no cash exchange). We'll provide a brief explanatory note to include with the donor flow.

Kim (Payroll): Implementation note: donors will see a PTO deduction on the next payroll cycle; recipients will get a coded PTO credit "PDO-APR" so HR systems stay auditable. We'll pilot in US/EU first, then expand.

Aisha (Eng Manager): Is there a cap per request? Could someone request 200 hours?

Luis (People Ops): Max per request = 160 hours. Managers can request multiple times across quarters with justification, subject to People Ops approval.

Nora (People Ops): On lactation accommodations: we're adding a dedicated booking system for private nursing rooms + an expanded flex scheduling policy (2x 30-min breaks or one 60-min break per 8-hour day) for 12 months postpartum. Facilities will add signage and supplies.

Ravi (Legal): This aligns with local statutory protections; we're keeping the policy at least as generous as local law and adding the reservation system to ensure room availability.

Kim (Payroll): Anything paid/compensated here is regular paid time. No change to salary or benefit deductions.

Aisha (Eng Manager): Appreciate the booking system  that should make it easier for teams to plan. Any guidance on cadence if multiple parents need the room at once?

Luis (People Ops): We recommend time-blocking and a team-first etiquette (shorter pump sessions where possible). If conflicts persist, People Ops can mediate and facilities will consider an additional room if demand is sustained.

HR-bot: PDO policy & form: https://intranet.redwood/workplace/policies/pdo-2026. Lactation accommodations: https://intranet.redwood/workplace/policies/lactation-2026. Booking: https://rooms.redwood/lactation.

Nora (People Ops): Rollout timeline: preview to managers today; employee comms 2026-10-15; manager training 2026-10-22 (15 min); PDO & lactation live 2026-11-01.

Aisha (Eng Manager): Will manager training include sample wording for team announcements?

Luis (People Ops): Yes, we'll include short email scripts and a 1-slide FAQ for team meetings.

Kim (Payroll): Payroll action: add PDO-APR code to payroll tool by 2026-10-25; sample run at end of Oct.

Ravi (Legal): We'll also update contractor/contingent worker guidance separately  contractors aren't eligible for PDO but may be supported case-by-case.

Nora (People Ops): Thanks all  please DM with any edge cases. If you're a manager with immediate need to donate time, contact People Ops and we'll process a manual donation this month. :heart:
